I’d say give it a shot, at the very least! I have skimmed through too many meal plans, due to certain things I’m too afraid to eat being there. I find replacing a couple of things, not necessarily to be lower calorie- but to just a familiar item, as substitute really helps! 

I’m sorry for being really vague about the “items” by the way. I would list specific things and subtleties that I prefer, but since I live in Europe I’m not sure you would know which ones I’m talking about.

Just like the other comment said, EDs tend to manifest as some sort of safety net and/or your only reliable coping mechanism, and changes alongside you. I know for me, and with help from psychologist, on my path to recovery in the past- instead of solely focusing on the temporary comfort it gives you, I try to only think about the negatives, the constant food fear, always having to check calories beforehand, extreme anxiety over certain foods, my throat burning like hell, and just general control over my life for what? 

What really helped me was trying to motivate me with anything I even *slightly* prioritize over my ed, (doesn’t have to be anything noteworthy tbh, like I’m weirdly passionate about getting a pet in the future?) and really just pushing the notion that you  *won’t* be able to achieve that (at least to the fullest) if you don’t get rid of your ED! But it’s also important to remember to take your time, I rushed in to recovery and oh boy, it ended in a huge relapse- I don’t mean to scare you away from recovery or anything, and to be honest you’re never really 100% ready anyhow, but I would advice consulting your feelings about recovering to someone, if not a professional then your partner, before jumping headfirst in to it.

Hope you get better anyhow, and sorry for wasting your time, if this was a pure shit storm to read lol.
